newsitem.title: GERMANY: DHL says Rhine hub could go to Germany.
newsitem.headline: DHL says Rhine hub could go to Germany.

text.p: DHL Worldwide Express GmbH, the German division of DHL International, said the disputed DHL Rhine Valley hub could come to Germany if no agreement were reached in France over its location.
Ulrich Hartmann, DHL managing director Germany, told Reuters in an interview: "Talks are continuing and it is completely open whether the hub goes to France or Germany."
DHL had planned to establish the hub at Strasbourg but this collapsed when the project was opposed by residents and local authorities.
Since then Nancy-Metz airport in the Lorraine region of France has offered to host the hub, as have other French airports.
Hartmann said: "Germany is certainly an option from the infrastructure and the availability of airports but the readiness of politicians is another question."
"There are a whole lot of airports used previously by the U.S. with large runways which are not used now and our aircraft are much quieter than those of the Americans," he said.
Hartmann suggested several airports in the Black Forest region were potential sites for the planned Rhine hub, which would serve eastern France and south-western Germany.
He did not name any individual airports, however.
Hartmann said DHL currently used a complex network of sub-hubs, including Frankfurt, Cologne and Nuremberg, for distribution throughout Germany.
The sub-hubs were served by air and road links from the main Brussels hub but also by direct connections to other European sub-hubs depending on volumes.
"Brussels is no longer such a hub for us. For example, when we have enough volume in Copenhagen for a direct flight to Germany, then we do that," he explained.
"In Europe, we use our own flights for about 90 percent (of consignments); internationally we have only flights to the U.S. and the rest is carried by commercial airlines.
"We have contracts with other carriers for blocked space. If we have a container space then we pay for it, even if the container is empty," he said.
DHL used flights of its partner Lufthansa Cargo AG but also of other airlines according to time needs, he added.
